MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JANUARY 22, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 6:35 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Susan Dueflas, Public Safety
  Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Gail Karish, BBK; Parker Davis, Media
  Technician; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk; and Travis Hart, Deputy Public Works
  Director

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chris Frost led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  January 12, 2024, with the amended agenda posted on January l8, 2024.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved to approve the agenda, hearing Item No. 6.F.
  after the consent calendar.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Riggins seconded the motion and moved to hear Item No. 6.B.
  after Item No. 7.A.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker of the motion.

FRIELDY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart moved to hear Item No. 6.D. after the consent calendar
  and before Item No. 6.F.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker and the seconder of the motion.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 22, 2024
  Page 2 of 11

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  ' Presentation
  of City Tile to Kelsey Pettijohn for Seven Years of Service to the City
  of Malibu

  Mayor Uhring presented the City Tile to City Clerk Pettijohn.

  City Clerk Pettijohn thanked the Council for the recognition.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS

  Pacific Coast Highway Safety Review
  Recommended Action: Receive and flle the January 2024 Pacific Coast Highway
  Safety Report and provide direction to explore traffic calming measurers pursuant
  to the Declaration of Emergency.

  Deputy City Manager Brown presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to- staff.

  Mayor Uhring opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Harris Hart, Margot Smit, Alexandria Andres, Michael Sugioto, Bridget
  Thompson, Brooke Doherty, Myers Mentzer, Kraig Hill, Jo Drummond, Ryan
  Embree, Barry Stewart, Robert Seltzer, Andy Lyon, and Georgia Goldfarb

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Uhring returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Uhring seconded a motion to direct
  staffto bring back a list of concrete actions the City can take to address PCH safety.

  The Council discussed the motion.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart moved to direct staff to bring back an item in six weeks
  identifying additional feasible PCH Safety Projects.

  The Council discussed the amendment.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker and seconder of the motion.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 22, 2024
  Page 3 of 11

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Tim Pera, MRCA Ranger, provided a ranger report for the last‘month. He stated
  224 parking citations were issued, and four citations were issued for dogs on the
  beach and alcohol at Lechuza Beach. He stated additional officers were scheduled
  to patrol during the holidays and no incidents occurred. He stated four
  administrative citations were issued at Escondido Canyon Trail for off-trail use in
  a closed area and two citations were issued for dogs off—leash.

  In responseto Councilmember Riggins, 'Mr. Pera stated the statistics reflected
  citations issued throughout the coastal division.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Mr. Pera stated MRCA Rangers also
  had the authority to pull over drivers for speeding.

  Bobby LaBonge asked if the City was coordinating with Ventura and Santa Monica
  on PCH safety items. He discussed the Topanga Beach underpass and suggested it
  be utilized more to keep people safe when crossing PCH.

  Mayor Uhring stated Los Angeles Councilmember Traci Park participated in the
  PCH tour with the Secretary of Transportation.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated the Mayor of Santa Monica also participated in the
  PCH tour with the Secretary of Transportation.

  Kraig Hill congratulated City Clerk Pettijohn. He suggested ways to address
  speeding on PCH, including bumper stickers and adding stop lights at entrances to
  the City. He discussed fractional ownership and taxes in Australia on unoccupied
  investment homes.

  Ryan Embree discusseda Public Safety Commission assignment in the early 2000s
  to discuss and evaluate a traffic mitigation fee for new development. He
  recommended implementing a traffic mitigation fee. He recommended the City
  direct Sheriff’s Deputies escort drivers through the city, similar to mountain towns
  with heavy snow conditions.

  Jo Drummond congratulated City Clerk Pettijohn. She stated the accident that
  killed four Pepperdine students was caused by a young male Malibu resident and
  discussed the importance of educating our students on driving safety. She thanked
  MRCA for clearing brush at Big Rock and PCH. She discussed weeding events at
  Point Dume Headlands every other Wednesday. She announced Malibu High
  School’s production of Frozen. She discussed’plans for Middle SchoolAthletics
  Pathway. She encouraged the public to attend the SM—MUSD districting meeting
  at the Santa Monica College Malibu campus.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 22, 2024
  Page 4 of 11

  Ted Vaill stated he was not recognized to speak on Item No. 6.A. because he
  submitted a speaker slip after the item was called. He indicated support for
  Councilmember Silverstein’s comments. He questioned why the Sheriff’s
  Department could not hire additional staff when CHP was hiring new officers. He
  questioned why the Malibu Film Society did not have a location in the City to host
  film screenings.

  Farnaz Gaminchi discussed a homeless encampment near Rambla Orienta. She
  discussed safety concerns related to the homeless encampment.
‘ ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary stated he attended a Las Virgenes-Malibu Council of
  Governments (COG) meeting where a fiber optic project was discussed. He
  discussed the Special City Council meeting on the draft housing element last week
  and stated public comment on the draft housing element was open through January
  24, 2024. He stated after public comment closed the draft housing element would
  be provided to the California Department ofHousing and Community Development
  (HCD). He stated he attended a screening of 21 Miles in Malibu and participated
  in a panel discussion with the filmmaker Michel Shane and Captain Jennifer Seetoo.
  He stated the event was hosted by Santa Monica College and the Community
  Services Department.

  Public Works Director DuBoux provided an update on the PCH Signal
  Synchronization Project. He stated the majority of the work going forward would
  be installing conduit on the land-side of PCH. He stated there were traffic control
  measures to ensure the work was completed safely, but it did have traffic impacts.
  He stated staff had submitted a new plan to Caltrans that would maintain two lanes
  of traffic in each direction.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Public Works Director DuBouX stated
  Caltrans had to approve traffic control measuresfor the project and they had been
  very‘accommodating for this project. He stated this project would not-have any
  night work. He stated staff could look into closing lanes at night.

  In response to Councilmember Riggins, Public Works Director DuBoux stated
  members of the public could sign up for traffic notifications through the City’s
  website.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Stewart, Public Works Director DuBoux discussed
  the challenges for this project that made night work impractical. He discussed the
  safety impacts.

  City Manager McClary stated the annual homeless count was scheduled for January
  24, 2024. He announced Mary Bradley had been brought on as the Interim Human
  Resources Manager. He announced a Los Angeles County Committee meeting on
  January 31, 2024 for a public hearing on SM-MUSD district elections. He stated
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes 0f January 22, 2024
  Page 5 of 11

  this hearing was unrelated to the City’s efforts to separate from SM-MUSD. He
  stated that the next Regular City Council meeting would be held in three weeks on
  February 12, 2024.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County SheriffDepartment, discussed a hit
  and run accident at Big Rock and stated a person of interest had been identified.
  He discussed an accident on January 11, 2024 near Duke’s Restaurant and stated
  DUI was suspected. He discussed a CHP pursuit that led through Malibu and led
  to an arrest. He stated that individual had bonded out. He discussed 2023 crime
  statistics. He stated there were 44 part one crimes in December 2023 and 476 part
  one crimes in 2023, down from 484 in 2022. He discussed an increase in vehicle
  burglaries at the beach and reminded members of the public not to leave valuables
  in their cars. He broke down crime statistics by age range and zip code and
  explained that majority of citations were issued to 20—34-year-olds and only 10%
  of citations were issued to residents in the 90265-zip code. He discussed a traffic
  stop with a speeding driver today.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Sergeant Soderlund stated the traffic
  stop did not involve a Malibu resident. He stated the individual pursued by CHP
  was a Malibu resident.

  Counc11member Sllversteln thanked Sergeant Soderlund for staylng for the durat1on
  of every CounCII meetlng

  Councilmember Grisanti discussed a homeless encampment near La Costa that may
  be on property owned by Los Angeles County.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated Public Safety staff may be working on the
  encampment near La Costa.

  Mayor Uhring requested a list of citations broken down by zip code.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he attended a Las Virgenes-Malibu Council of
  Governments meeting and the 21 Miles in Malibu screening. He stated Malibu was
  21 miles long in a straight line, but it was a 27‘mile long drive on PCH.

  Councilmember Riggins stated she attended the 21 Miles in Malibu screening. She
  stated Malibu High School (MHS) had a safe driving event Every 15 Minutes every
  few years She dlscussed Klan and Joel Schulman s work on earth friendly
  management p011c1es 1n other Cltles She announced tree plantlng events at
  Topanga and Encmal Flats With the Resource Conservation District of the Santa
  Monica Mountains. She encouraged Malibu and County residents to get a home
  hardening assessment from the City of Malibu or the Resource Conservation
  District. She announced the Agents of Discovery program launching at Legacy
  Park and encouraged the public to download the app.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes 0f January 22, 2024
  Page 6 of 11

  Councilmember Silverstein stated he had been researching PCH safety issues. He
  stated he attended the 21 Malibu in Malibu screening. He stated the Council had
  taken actions to help the Malibu Film Society find a venue in the City and make
  their screenings available to all residents in Malibu, but it had not worked out. He
  stated under the City’s emergency declaration the City had the authority to enact a
  curfew and suggested implementing a curfew that prevented people from driving
  on PCH unless they were driving to or from their home.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Grisanti stated Los
  Angeles County owned the property with the homeless encampment near La Costa.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the City’s no camping ordinance and how it
  can be enforced. He stated the individual camping near La Costa was violating the
  City’s law. He suggested the City of Malibu file an amicus brief in the City of
  Grants Pass V. Johnson case. He discussed how Malibu attracted individuals
  experiencing homelessness who had never lived in Malibu.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart indicated support for sending an amicus brief.

l]
  Councilmember Grisanti discussed the negative attention Malibu sometimes .
  received when it attached its name to an issue. He questioned ifthe City’s lobbyist
  California Strategies would recommend filing a brief.

  In response to Councilmember Riggins, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated he
  believed the League 0f California Cities was filinga brief and discussed briefs by
  other cities.

  CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to consider filing an
  amicus brief for the City of Grants Pass v. Johnson case.

  In response to Councilmember Grisanti’s comments, Councilmember Silverstein
  stated he did not see Malibu becoming the subject of derision on this issue when
  many other officials and agencies had a similar position.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated he attended the 21 Miles in Malibu screening. He
  discussed law enforcement officer recruitments and the limit on academy class
  sizes. He stated he attended a Los Angeles County City Selection Committee
  meeting on behalf of the Mayor. He stated he attended the homeless outreach
  community meeting. He stated he attended an Administration and Finance
  Subcommittee meeting to discuss an item for vacant land outreach.

  Mayor Uhring stated he attended the 21 Miles in Malibu screening. He expressed
  concern that more children would be visiting Legacy Park for the Agents of
  Discovery program when there were individuals experiencing homelessness in the
  park.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 22, 2024
  Page 7 of 11

  Councilmember Riggins stated City staff would be present at the event on Sunday
  and she did not expect children to have issues visiting the park with their parents
  during daytime hours.

  Mayor Uhring opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Ryan Embree and Jo Drummond

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Uhring returned the matter
